==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/læk/|a=RP,GA}} * {{audio|en|En-us-lack.ogg|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-lack.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{homophones|en|lakh|qq1=one pronunciation}} * {{rhymes|en|æk|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|lack}}, {{m|enm|lakke}}, {{m|enm|lak}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*læc|t=deficiency, lack, want}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lak}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*laką}}, {{m|gem-pro|*lakaz|t=slackness}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lakaz|t=limp, slack, loose, low}}, related to {{m|gem-pro|*lak(k)ōną|t=to blame, reproach}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lok-néh₂-}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Lak|t=lack}}, {{cog|gml|lack}}, {{m|gml|lak|t=lack}}, {{cog|nl|lak|t=lack, deficiency, calumny}}, {{cog|is|lakur||lacking}}. Related also to {{cog|dum|laken|t=to blame, lack}}. Eclipsed non-native {{ncog|enm|carence|t=absence, lack}}, from {{ncog|fro|carence}}. Unrelated to {{ncog|la|lacuna|t=gap, void, want}}, itself from {{ncog|la|lacus|t=lake, pond}}, ultimately from {{ncog|ine-pro|*lókus}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # A [[deficiency]] or [[need]] (of something desirable or necessary); an [[absence]], [[want]], [[dearth]]. #: {{syn|en|paucity|}} #: {{antonyms|en|glut|surplus|plethora}} #: {{ux|en|It is a question of money, or '''lack''' of same.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|IV|1|text={{...}} let his '''lack''' of years be no impediment to let him lack a reverend estimation;}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 7, 2012|author=Phil McNulty|work=BBC Sport |title=[http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19460608 Moldova 0-5 England] |passage=If Moldova harboured even the slightest hopes of pulling off a comeback that would have bordered on miraculous given their '''lack''' of quality, they were snuffed out 13 minutes before the break when {{w|Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain|Oxlade-Chamberlain}} picked his way through midfield before releasing {{w|Jermain Defoe|Defoe}} for a finish that should have been dealt with more convincingly by {{w|Stanislav Namașco|Namasco}} at his near post.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[defect]] or [[failing]]; moral or spiritual degeneracy. #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=1|passage=In the old days, to my commonplace and unobserving mind, he gave no evidences of genius whatsoever. He never read me any of his manuscripts, […], and therefore my '''lack''' of detection of his promise may in some degree be pardoned.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col2|en|for lack of|for lack of trying|lack of sleep|lackless}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|deficiency, need}} * Albanian: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Assamese: * Azerbaijani: * Belarusian: * Bhojpuri: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * German: * Gothic: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Ladino: * Latin: * Macedonian: * Malayalam: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|отсу́тствие|n}}, {{t+|ru|нехва́тка|f}}, {{t+|ru|недоста́ток|m}}, {{t+|ru|нужда́|f}} {{qualifier|need}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tocharian B: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Urdu: * Welsh: * Yiddish: * Zazaki: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|lacken}}, {{m|enm|lakken}}, {{m|enm|laken}}, from {{inh|en|ang|læccian}}, {{m|ang|*lacian|t=to blame, criticise, lack}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lak(k)ōn|t=to blame, be lacking}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lak(k)ōną|t=to reproach, blame, be lacking}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lok-néh₂-}}. Cognate with {{cog|ofs|lakia}}, {{m|ofs|lekia|t=to contest, blame}}, {{cog|gml|lacken}}, {{m|gml|laken|t=to reproach, blame, criticise}}, {{cog|dum|laken|t=to disapprove, blame, lack}}, {{cog|nl|laken|t=to blame, reproach}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive|stative}} To be [[without]], not to have, to need, to [[require]]. #: {{ux|en|My life '''lacks''' excitement.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be short (''of'' or ''for'' something). #: {{ux|en|He'll never '''lack''' for company while he's got all that money.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|I|4|text=''Hamlet''. What hour now?
''Horatio''. I think it '''lacks''' of twelve.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To be in [[want]]. #* {{RQ:KJV|Psalms|34|10|text=The young lions do '''lack''', and suffer hunger {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To see the [[deficiency]] in (someone or something); to [[find fault]] with, to [[malign]], [[reproach]]. #* {{RQ:Langland Piers Plowman|II|text=That is Mede þe Mayde quod she · hath noyed me ful oft / And '''ylakked''' my lemman.}} # {{lb|en|AAVE}} To be [[off one's guard]]. #: {{ux|en|His opps caught him '''lacking'''.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|alack|lackbrain|lackland|lacklustre|lackstock |lack-all|lack-grace|lack-latin|lack-laughter|lack-learning|lack-life|lack-linen|lack-looks|lack-love|lack-mind|lack-pity|lackwit}} =====Related terms===== * {{l|en|lackluster}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|be without, need, require}} * Albanian: * Asturian: * Basque: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Faliscan: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Greenlandic: * Haitian Creole: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kashubian: * Khmer: * Korean: * Ladino: * Latin: * Macedonian: * Māori: * Mongolian: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Old Church Slavonic: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Quechua: * Russian: {{t+|ru|отсу́тствовать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|недостава́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|недоста́ть|pf}}, {{t+|ru|нужда́ться|impf}} (''need'') * Sidamo: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Vietnamese: * Welsh: * Wolaytta: * Yup'ik: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 3=== ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{archaic form of|en|lakh}}. #: ''a '''lack''' of rupees'' ===Further reading=== * {{R:gem:EDPG|lak(k)on-|325}} ===See also=== * [[good lack]] ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=ackl|calk|kcal}}
